stage: M77 planned: shared versus context-dependent native input-to-write computation
question: Do useful global output spans correspond to a shared linear map from normalized MLP inputs, or are the changes generated by context-dependent bilinear operators?
theory: For the pinned bias-free Left/Right layers, F(z)=D[(Lz)*(Rz)] is homogeneous quadratic. J(z)v=D[(Lz)*(Rv)+(Lv)*(Rz)]. Exactly F(zd)-F(zr)=J((zd+zr)/2)(zd-zr). Down bias cancels. Here J is the native MLP input-to-write Jacobian, not the downstream logit Jacobian of M74. z is the normalized MLP input; no derivative through normalization is included because endpoint z is supplied.
reference: Capture native MLP1 normalized inputs on natural training docs0–31. Use exactly the4092 M7 unique-prefix training indices to compute float64 mean z. Hash indices/mean/captures; no task/evaluation data enters this reference. The mean and pair midpoint may be off the RMS sphere: they are algebraic anchors of the quadratic map, not claims of natural hidden states.
implementation: Evaluate analytic J(z)v without materializing a full tensor, using pinned L/R/Down weights. Independent explicit small-matrix/Jacobian and finite-difference toy checks before native evaluation. On native captures verify endpoint product difference and midpoint equality with stated numerical tolerances before downstream scoring.
toys: Fixed linear-on-an-affine-slice and context-dependent product functions; duplicated and cancelling channel implementations of the same function must have identical functional Jacobians despite different channel-removal behavior. Use deterministic seeds and all declared toy cases; no toy outcome-based model selection.
cohort: All56M75pairs/sevenfamilies, both endpoints, source/final/identity; preserve8source ineligibilities and native competence qualification. No featurizer fitting, task labels in training, rank truncation or norm matching. Shared and recipient predictors use donor-recipient normalized-input differences, so they are conditional change models, not full token-to-output language models.
evaluation: Patch each predicted write change into the native recipient background. Replay teacher/native outputs; report all raw/equal-family/pooled/margin/local errors and formats. Exact midpoint control should replay native targets to numerical tolerance. Compare shared versus recipient and exact controls, without selecting tasks or sites after outcomes.
deliverable: A bounded decision for executable featurizer design: shared linear input coordinates versus context-conditioned local/bilinear structure. Do not mistake output compression for computing the MLP, or expansion-point term cancellation for native channel cancellation.
stop: One three-predictor diagnostic and fixed toy validation. No additional anchor/rank/amplitude search. Return to an explicit input-to-write representation or targeted reusable-component test based on this result; retain whole-task training exclusions.
